R308 — bounded segmented serve route synchronization review
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)
Source: XeStrata pristine b9f00e9db7fd56decdd9930ee84049d980b904e4; old comparison pin da3d426079019daa6e01388d03b0d94ae67070b7. Worktree: /home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/MistVVK/XeStrata/.worktree/bench-xestrata-b9f00e9-pristine-20261013.
Scope: source-only route audit for one Intel Arc B570, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, bounded ordinary --serve operation. No build, test, device query, import, Git mutation, server/model run, GPU work, or cleanup. This does not claim runtime validation.

Exact route and decision
For the listed no-batch, no-MTP serve configuration, I found no reachable host/device concurrent volatile poll or host/device atomic operation on the forced segmented verifier path. The earlier R306 concern applies to the one-shot session_loop/session_run_token route, which ordinary --serve does not enter: the serve block returns at src/program/generate.cpp:10854-10855; the one-shot session token calls are below it at 11044-11062. Serving requests use Verifier::run and the server prompt reader.
This is a source-level synchronization finding for the stated configuration. It relies on the forced adapter's stream synchronization and queue submission correctly ordering accesses to mapped host-USM; exact Arc B570 runtime capability and fault evidence remain uncollected.

Relevant configuration
Arguments: --serve, --batch unset/0, --pipeline-windows default 1, no MTP artifacts, --spec4, --short-read 0, --prefill 8192, --pcie-frac 0, --adapt-swaps 0, --conversation-cache-mib 0, --prompt-cache 0, --suffix-draft 0.
Environment: STRATA_VERIFY_SEGMENTED=1, STRATA_VERIFY_DEVICE_PLAN=0, STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0, STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_GATE=0, STRATA_PREFILL_ISSUER=0, STRATA_ARENA_HOST_USM=1, STRATA_PREFILL_FIRST=0, STRATA_COPY_ENGINE=0, EnableDirectSubmission=0, STRATA_EVENT_MARK=barrier; use the previously qualified nativeUR_L0v2 adapter. Set these before process startup. STRATA_PREFILL_FIRST has no reference in the reviewed b9 source tree, so it does not select a route at this pin.
For a deterministic segmented-path diagnosis, add STRATA_VERIFY_RESIDENT_GRAPH=0. Its default is on when all experts are resident and the source can select a separate resident graph, bypassing segmentation. That path also has no host expert service/doorbell: recording_res_ suppresses doorbell_publish and its resident plan is built on device. Forcing it off ensures this review addresses the intended segmented CPU-share route.

Route trace
- Startup / tuning: Verifier::init calls tune_device (src/core/verify.cpp:462-464, 253-264); for GDN shapes it tunes device-only scratch graphs, fetch_blobs_tune (src/kernels/xe/verify_kernels.cpp:547-590, 944-970) briefly has a kernel read a host-USM source buffer after the host has filled it and leaves it unchanged through q.wait, and BF16 GEMV tuning uses device scratch (src/kernels/xe/bf16_gemv.cpp:372-410). generate.cpp may call the same cached tuning again at 5020-5030. No doorbell-visibility probe is invoked: verify.cpp:495-496 uses the explicit STRATA_VERIFY_SEGMENTED value instead of calling doorbell_visible().
- READY and capture: READY is emitted at src/program/generate.cpp:7622-7624 after initialization/tuning. The first request's Verifier::run captures its T-token graph lazily at verify.cpp:1553-1554; capture splits the graph around each expert-service boundary at 1274-1291 and ends with a stream sync at 1420-1433. Capture records work but does not execute the captured doorbell kernel.
- Prompt: --short-read 0 is explicit, so windows_ok allows zero fresh tokens through verifier windows only; prompt parts are read by the batched prompt path. With --batch off, read_part calls sp.run directly (generate.cpp:9405-9412; selection at 9604-9618). STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0 makes cpu_share_on false at prefill.cpp:137-145 and cpu_maybe false at 1833-1841, so the prompt's expert products stay on the GPU. The threaded stager can still copy immutable expert blobs to pinned ring buffers: its ready/head/issued atomics are C++ host-thread atomics (prefill.cpp:315-370), with reuse gated by event_sync/event_record and copy completion (331-339, 372-375; issuance around 1435-1452). It is not a device kernel spinning on these atomics. There is no launch_host in prefill.cpp.
- Last prompt token and decode: the serve loop sets p=n-1 and x to the last prompt token (generate.cpp:9690-9695). With no MTP and --suffix-draft 0, T is 1 for the first and subsequent windows: generation chooses use_mtp ? S_mtp : 1 at 10328-10334; only suffix drafts can enlarge it (10339-10345). So --spec4 is the verifier's maximum window allocation, not a four-token speculative window in this no-MTP route. Each decode calls ver.run at 10401 and commits at 10439.
- Segmented verifier ownership: verify.cpp:495-500 selects segmentation explicitly. run launches segment zero, then calls stream_sync(cs_) before reading h_seq/doorbell payload at 1623-1627. The kernel's doorbell_publish writes payload and increments seq (verify.cpp:1100-1102; elementwise.cpp:216-233), but the host reads it only after that segment is complete. CPU pool work reads the published payload and writes plan/flags at 1643-1663. post() in segmented mode copies the now-published plan and omits device waits on flagA, flagB and CPU-result flag at 1158-1169, 1200-1204, 1230-1241. Before launching the next segment, run syncs copy_ and verifies flagB at 1664-1671. Thus there is no kernel concurrently polling the host seq/flags while the host reads or writes them. The next segment's plan/flag reads occur only after the host writes and subsequent launch; in the late-PLE case pre(layer 1) does have wait_flag_ge(m_flag_,1) at 644-647, but the host gather and flag publication precede that segment launch (1578, 1596-1612, 1663-1671).
- PCIe and callbacks: explicit --pcie-frac 0 is parsed as given; setup_pcie_split then does not install its measured split (generate.cpp:1770-1783). The serve request sets pcie_num to zero (9523-9524), so no PCIe-share experts are dispatched. Even if a zero-count fetch reaches fetch_dma, it only performs a host-side raise_flag and returns at verify.cpp:1791-1795; the asynchronous launch_host callback is used only for positive n at 1796-1801. More generally, segmented mode skips the kernel's pcie flag wait and drains copy_ before relaunch, so that callback's flag would not be polled by a running kernel.
- Flags and atomics: verifier host buffers (including seq, flag, flagA/B and payload) are mapped allocations at verify.cpp:344-360. The host's h_seq/flag volatile resets occur before graph launch (1578-1592), and the final output read follows stream sync (1677-1706). The device's plain volatile ring store has a system fence, but no host observes it concurrently in this segmented route. The device system-scope atomic in doorbell_visible is not run because the environment overrides that probe. The optional host/device system-scope GDN debug atomic_ref is inside the STRATA_DBG_GDN diagnostic helper (verify_kernels.cpp:603-630) and is not enabled here. Device-scope atomics used within kernels, such as row reduction, are device-memory synchronization and are outside this host-USM hazard (verify_kernels.cpp:1148-1169). The host-only __atomic compare-exchange in raise_flag (verify.cpp:1782-1785) is not a device atomic and with pcie_frac 0 no positive-count callback invokes it asynchronously.

Safety prerequisites and limits
1. Preserve STRATA_VERIFY_SEGMENTED=1 in the launched process; a build or wrapper that drops it re-enters the unqualified volatile doorbell poll path.
2. Set STRATA_VERIFY_RESIDENT_GRAPH=0 to guarantee the intended segmented behavior; otherwise an all-resident model/cache can take a different, no-host-service graph route. This is a determinism prerequisite, not a finding that the resident route is unsafe.
3. Keep batch=0, pipeline-windows=1, no MTP artifacts, short-read=0, suffix-draft=0, and pcie-frac=0. Batch and pipelined verifier paths explicitly reject segmented mode (verify.cpp:1836, 2491), and re-enabling these features changes the graph/host ownership analysis.
4. Do not add STRATA_DBG_GDN=1 or an alternate diagnostic that calls doorbell_visible() with its explicit concurrent host/device poll. Do not interpret ordinary host-USM expert-data reads as control-word polling; the stager's host buffer lifetime is event-gated.
5. This review assumes the forced nativeUR_L0v2 adapter's stream_sync/queue launch semantics, and does not validate its behavior on this B570. Main must still record the actual device, driver, Level Zero adapter/compiler versions, allocation/atomic aspects, launch status and kernel/OS fault checks before treating an on-card run as qualified. Do not claim measured correctness or performance from this source review.

Reviewed code paths are pinned to b9f00e9db7fd56decdd9930ee84049d980b904e4; this review does not amend R306 or make any repository-source change.
